_notes.MISSING: produced by every tree-sitter parser and not a construct: tree-sitter marks an ABSENT required token with `isMissing` on the TOKEN'S OWN type, so the string "MISSING" is never a node type a fixture can contain — a `handled_verified` row would read `uncovered: MISSING` forever. The lane's error walk does read `isMissing` off the whole tree (real-groovy-analyzer.ts:184-185); every lane in the fleet records that read with this same row, so the class is named here rather than claimed. A node type that no fixture can witness is not evidence, and a bucket has to say which of the two it means.

decisions.node_type: heritage targets with folded type arguments (implements Cache<T>)
decisions.question: The pinned groovy grammar folds type args into the supertype token text (`implements Cache<T>` -> super_interfaces child text `Cache<T>`). deriveTreeEdges pushed the raw token, but decls keys are bracket-stripped at registration (M37.9) — the implements edge could never match its interface, nested-interface override chains died silently (geb CachingDriverFactory: SimpleCache.get -> Cache.get surfaced unexplained @150).

Mutant groovy/heritage-typeargs-revert re-brackets Cache -> Cache<T> and must die.

decisions.question: An anonymous class body registers a symbol, a symbolMap key and a scope (with `parents: [constructedType]`) — does it also enter `classHierarchy`, which is the ONLY map the override pass reads?

decisions.question: Which source form produces the grammar's `lambda_expression` node, and what is the contract for it? (M14.0.F6 read uncovered: [lambda_expression], i.e. an analyzer branch with no fixture.)
decisions.resolution: The UNBRACED arrow — `(int x) -> x + 1`, `s -> !s.isEmpty()`, `() -> x`, `(K k, V v) -> { … }` — parenthesised or not, typed or not; every BRACE form (`{ x -> x + 1 }`, `{ int x -> x + 1 }`, `{ x + 1 }`, `{ a, b -> a + b }`, `list.each { int x -> print x }`) is a `closure`. It is REAL, mainstream syntax, not an exotic spelling: 60 occurrences in 26 files across the two pinned corpora, with the parent a variable_declarator (26), argument_list (20), expression_statement (8), range_expression (3), closure (2) or return_statement (1) — `.filter(s -> !s.isEmpty())`, `map.forEach((K key, V value) -> { … })`, `registerBean(…, () -> userCacheManager)`. CONTRACT (family, K6/#866): a lambda is an EXPRESSION — no symbol of its own, its parameters are not project symbols, and the calls in its body (including an argument-position lambda's) attribute to the lexically enclosing declaration at their own lines. Pinned by fixture groovy/lambda-expression.

excluded.label: renders
excluded.from: **=> THE CLASS IS ONTOLOGICAL, AND THE REASON IS THE ENUM'S OWN CONTRACT - NOT A LADDER RUNG.** A VOCABULARY RULING IS NOT A GRAMMAR MATTER: no R1, R2 or R3 of the remedy ladder could conjure another language's construct into `.groovy` text, and naming a rung for it would misdescribe the reason. `src/ast/types.ts` - the enum's OWN CONTRACT for `renders`: "A component RENDERS another component: source = the rendering symbol, target = the rendered component. Measured population is TSX/JSX (`<Button/>` inside a component)" => THE CONTRACT'S SUBJECT IS A COMPONENT RENDERING A COMPONENT. **=> THE NEAR-MISS CENSUS IS KEPT, IN TWO HALVES, AND BOTH ARE COUNTED.** (1) **THE OTHER DIALECT'S DIALECT: 683 Grails `.gsp` server-page templates in grails-core DO render components** (`<g:render>`, `<g:include>`), and they are NOT this lane's files: the M60 #913 ruling (2026-09-24) stopped routing `.gsp` to groovy because a Grails Server Page is an HTML document carrying `${}`/`<g:...>` tags and `<%--%>` comments, the Groovy grammar has no productions for it, and 39 of 39 sampled grails-core files parse with ERROR nodes (`src/ast/language-detection.ts`, the `.gsp` entry). (2) **THE IN-LANGUAGE NEAREST NEIGHBOUR: 98 `template_expression` nodes** over the admitted population - a Groovy GString interpolation renders a VALUE into a string, not a COMPONENT into a page, so it is not the relation the value names. => AND THE GRAMMAR-SIDE HALF IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: the SERVED build's node-type census names 163 named node types and **0** of them carries a render-ish name (`validation/m14/measurements/groovy-grammar-nodes.json`). => THE COUNTER: `script/m14/groovy-population-census.ts` (the `template_expression` and the `.gsp` counts), run over the admitted population - 8102 admitted files across ? repositories.

excluded.label: part_of
excluded.from: **=> THE GRAMMAR HAS NO SUCH CONSTRUCT, AND THE HALF THAT MAKES THIS AN EXCLUSION RATHER THAN AN UNIMPLEMENTED TYPE IS MEASURED.** A LANE THAT MERELY LACKS AN EMISSION SITE HAS AN UNIMPLEMENTED TYPE - a GAP, and a gap does not shrink the denominator. => WHAT SHRINKS IT IS THAT THE LANGUAGE DOES NOT EXPRESS THE TYPE AT ALL. THE GRAMMAR-SIDE HALF: the SERVED build's node-type census (`validation/m14/measurements/groovy-grammar-nodes.json`, 163 named node types, id-ORDER digest bf14e3776f4df1b307ac09c7bcb8d7a9ff1d43e26c73c5f32cb5160859599eb6) names **0** node types carrying a `part` shape, and the contract's subject is a LIBRARY UNIT INCLUDING A PART FILE - Dart's `part 'x.dart'` / `part of` (`src/ast/types.ts`) - which Groovy has no syntax for. => THE NEAR-MISS CENSUS IS COUNTED: **47** occurrences of the `part '<file>'` / `part of` token shapes over the admitted population (`script/m14/groovy-population-census.ts`). => THE COUNTER AND THE POPULATION: `script/m14/groovy-population-census.ts` over the admitted set - 8102 admitted files across ? repositories, ? over the 1 MB cap, ? tracked-but-absent, 137 symlinked directories corpus-wide of which **0** are followed by the git-tracked walk.

excluded.label: mixes_in
excluded.from: **=> THIS IS A GROOVY QUESTION, AND THE ANSWER IS MEASURED IN GROOVY.** Groovy HAS traits: **165 trait declarations** over the admitted population (`script/m14/groovy-population-census.ts`), and a trait is applied in EXACTLY TWO WAYS, and BOTH ARE ALREADY PUBLISHED: **1030** applications through an `implements` clause and **32** through an `extends` clause. => **=> AND THERE IS NO THIRD FORM, AND THE PARSE TREE IS WHY: a trait application is written as an ORDINARY `implements` entry - `super_interfaces` -> `type_list` -> `type_identifier` - with NO grammar-level distinction from an interface implementation** (measured on the served build: `class Service implements Audited, Serializable` parses with `Audited` as a plain `type_identifier`; the SERVED build's census names 0 mixin-ish node types among its 163). => **=> AND THE TIE-BREAK THAT MAKES THIS A RULING AND NOT A PREFERENCE IS THE ENUM'S OWN CONTRACT.** `mixes_in` exists because in Dart a mixin is NEITHER `extends` NOR `implements` - "no conformance is declared" (`src/ast/types.ts`) - **and IN GROOVY THE CONFORMANCE IS DECLARED**, so the `implements` edge is the TRUTHFUL one and there is no construct left for `mixes_in` to name. => **=> A CONSTRUCT THAT IS EXPRESSIBLE IN THE SAME WAY AS AN ALREADY-IMPLEMENTED TYPE IS NOT A NEW TYPE - IT IS THAT TYPE, SPELLED DIFFERENTLY.** => THE FALSIFIER, WITH ITS COUNT: if the admitted population carried a class that composed a trait WITHOUT declaring a conformance and WITHOUT a single base - a `with`-shaped clause - the ruling would be false; **COUNTED: 165 trait declarations, 1030 applications by `implements`, 32 by `extends`, and 0 applications in any third form** (`script/m14/groovy-population-census.ts`).

coverage._from: DERIVATION. implemented = the eleven types with an emission site in src/ast/real-groovy-analyzer.ts, named per type in `_emissionSites`: the ten canonical types plus `decorates` (the publication post-pass, src/ast/real-groovy-analyzer.ts:515). THE PINNED GRAMMAR carries every one of them: wasm/tree-sitter-groovy.wasm (sha256 f1e68cb398e6), 163 named node types, id-ORDER digest bf14e3776f4df1b307ac09c7bcb8d7a9ff1d43e26c73c5f32cb5160859599eb6 (validation/m14/measurements/groovy-grammar-nodes.json). THE THREE EXCLUSIONS, EACH WITH A CLASS, A COUNT AND A CITATION: renders (ontological - the enum's own contract names a COMPONENT rendering a COMPONENT, and the near miss is counted in two halves), part_of (grammar-absence - 0 of the 163 named node types carries a `part` shape, and the `part`/`part of` token shapes are counted), mixes_in (ontological - Groovy HAS traits (165 trait declarations) but a trait is applied EITHER by `implements` (1030) or by `extends` (32), both already published, and the enum's own contract says a mixin is the thing that is NEITHER). NO TYPE IS IN GRAMMAR REMEDY PENDING, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT THE LANE, NOT A ROUTE AROUND THE GATE: a pending type stays in the denominator and is counted as an unimplemented gap, so a lane cannot improve its ratio by declaring work in flight. CLOSURE: implemented 11 + corpusUnexercised 0 + gaps 0 = applicable 11 = 14 - 3 excluded. THE MEASUREMENT: the fleet's own instrument, `script/m14/incoming-gate.ts groovy groovy,gvy,gradle 2000 --index --offset=N`, over the whole admitted population in DISJOINT SLICES of the gate's own sorted admitted list, merged by `script/m14/groovy-arm-merge.ts`; the per-slice outputs are validation/m14/measurements/groovy-arm/chunk-{0,2000,4000,6000,8000}.txt and the merged closure is validation/m14/measurements/groovy-arm-closure-2026-10-22.json. THE EDGE BUCKETS ARE THE POPULATION'S (every admitted file is measured exactly once, and an edge is a per-file fact); THE RESOLUTION BUCKETS ARE THE CHUNKED MEASUREMENT'S, AND `resolved` IS BIASED UP, because the resolution scope is PER PROJECT and a repository longer than one slice straddles a slice boundary — the bias is STATED WITH THE NUMBERS rather than bounded by assertion.

_implemented_measured._unit: THE WHOLE ADMITTED POPULATION, IN 5 DISJOINT SLICES OF THE GATE'S OWN SORTED ADMITTED LIST. THE ADMITTED SET is the git-tracked set (`git ls-files`) restricted to the router's extensions (.groovy, .gvy, .gradle — the incoming-gate's own router-verified table, script/m14/incoming-gate.ts:312) and to files under the 1 MB cap; the REPO COUNT is the repositories carrying an admitted file. INSTRUMENT: `script/m14/incoming-gate.ts groovy groovy,gvy,gradle 2000 --index --offset=N`; the per-slice outputs are validation/m14/measurements/groovy-arm/chunk-{0,2000,4000,6000,8000}.txt; the merge is script/m14/groovy-arm-merge.ts and the merged closure is validation/m14/measurements/groovy-arm-closure-2026-10-22.json. THE RESOLUTION BUCKETS ARE THE CHUNKED MEASUREMENT'S, AND `resolved` IS BIASED UP — the resolution scope is PER PROJECT and a repository longer than one slice STRADDLES a slice boundary, so the split half cannot see the collisions in the other half, and a collision that is INVISIBLE makes the name read UNIQUE and the edge RESOLVE. THE BIAS IS STATED WITH THE NUMBERS RATHER THAN BOUNDED BY ASSERTION.

denominator.rule: **THE DENOMINATOR IS THE LANGUAGE'S OWN EXPRESSIBLE SET, AND A PENDING TYPE IS EXPRESSIBLE — THAT IS PRECISELY WHY A RUNG IS AVAILABLE AND BEING TAKEN.** ⇒ A type in GRAMMAR REMEDY PENDING STAYS IN THE DENOMINATOR AND IS COUNTED AS AN UNIMPLEMENTED GAP, so the lane reads n-implemented/n, NOT n/n. The deciding argument is the INCENTIVE: if a pending type left the denominator, a lane could improve its own ratio by DECLARING WORK IN FLIGHT INSTEAD OF DOING IT — the julia-lane failure the coverage-block gate was written to prevent. ⇒ THIS LANE HAS NO PENDING TYPE: every type in the denominator is IMPLEMENTED, and the three types outside it are there because the LANGUAGE DOES NOT EXPRESS THEM, each with a class, a count and a citation. ⇒ THE CLOSURE: implemented 11 + corpusUnexercised 0 + gaps 0 = applicable 11 = 14 - 3 excluded (renders, part_of, mixes_in).
